paraphrase: The object-condition of sense-cognition cannot be atoms: though atoms might be its cause, cognition does not bear their image, so they are not its object, like the sense faculty; nor can it be the aggregate of atoms, which bears the image but, not being a real substance, is not a cause — like the double moon.
notes: Checked against the local e-text, which is a modern Sanskrit restoration (Aiyaswami Shastri) — no original quoted.

paraphrase: The object is the knowable form that is internal and appears as if external, because it is of the nature of consciousness and because it is its condition.
notes: Checked against the local restored-Sanskrit e-text.

paraphrase: The object is a condition as one part (of cognition), passing on a potency, either simultaneously or successively; the sense faculty is that potency (within consciousness), assisted by co-operating factors; object-form and potency condition each other from beginningless time.
notes: Checked against the local restored-Sanskrit e-text; condensed.
